symbols.name: LuxonDateTimeTransformer
symbols.sig: const LuxonDateTimeTransformer: ValueTransformer = { to(value: DateTime | null | undefined): Date | null { if (!value) return null; return value.toJSDate(); }, …
doc: I use this ValueTransformer to bridge the native JS Dates from the database to Luxon DateTime objects across the Next.js application layer.

members.name: holidayType
decos: @Column({ type: "enum", enum: HolidayType, name: "holidayType", nullable: false, })

members.name: categories
doc: Which employee categories this specific FH instance applies to (e.g. "A,B" or "B"). Only meaningful for FH rows: null for CH (applies to everyone) and for RH (there the categories' entitlement is a quota, not a per-holiday fact -- see the separate holiday_rh_quota table).

members.name: note
doc: Free-text annotation for anything noteworthy about THIS YEAR'S instance of a holiday. Currently used for one-off conditional reclassifications: e.g. 2024's circular additionally counts Ram Navami (normally an RH) as a Festival Holiday for Category B only, because Vijaya Dashami fell on their 2nd Saturday off-day that year, to keep their FH total at 18; 2026's circular does the same thing with Bengali New Year's Day instead, for the same reason (SAIL Foundation Day falling on a 4th Saturday). I represent it as a SECOND holidayyear row for the same holidayMasterId and year, with holidayType = FH and this note explaining why -- the existing RH row for that same master/year is untouched. Null for ordinary rows.
